title: Japan 2-year JGB auction (No.490 inferred) — the second of the two issues that close the 1-5y menu's 2-Year coupon channel
source: EST: mof.go.jp English October 2026 auction calendar (policy/jgbs/auction/calendar/2610e.htm), fetched direct 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 24,854 bytes) — its table row reads 'Oct. 29, 2026 | 2-year'. Both the announcement and result cells are the plain string 'Detail' with no href, so nothing about this auction has been published yet; MOF announces a 2-Year at D-7, so its terms publish about 2026-10-22. The '(No.490)' is an INFERENCE, not MOF's print — the calendar prints an issue number only once announced. Reproduced from MOF's own 2026 calendars 2601e-2610e (10 x HTTP 200), whose 2-Year rows run No.481 Jan. 30 through No.488 Aug. 28, one issue per calendar month with no gap, with Sep. 30 and Oct. 29 rows following. Filed `estimate` on this lane's no-self-confirm limit and because market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no slot for a non-US sovereign debt office; the date is MOF's own and is not in doubt. Discovered 2026-09-09 during the never-assessed initial research of jgb-2y-auction-2026-09-30
notes: PROPOSED because the proposer's own headline call cannot be scored without it, not because it completes a calendar. The 2026-11-20 liquidity-enhancement menu's 2-Year window advances by exactly +2 at both ends (No.476-488 becomes No.478-490 on the family's own 7-of-7 rule), so TWO issues enter it: No.489 from 2026-09-30 and No.490 from this auction. The proposer's finding is that the 2-Year sector reaches 100% >=1% coupon on that roll — every remaining known issue, No.478-488, is already >=1.0%, and the last sub-1% holdout No.476 (0.9%, 2,599.8bn) departs. That claim survives only if BOTH entrants price at >=1.0%, so a coupon on this print is half the test; registering only 2026-09-30 would leave the forward test half-blind. The cushion is wide — the 2Y CME yield was 1.848% on 2026-09-08 (MOF jgbcme.csv), about 90bp above the 0.95% level at which a coupon would round below 1.0% — but boj-decision-2026-09-18 sits between today and both auctions and the 2Y has run +19bp since 2026-08-14, so the cushion is an observation, not an assumption. Secondary value: the coupon rule this lane tested (coupon = the 2Y CME close rounded to the nearest 0.1%, 7 of 8 on the prior session's close, 8 of 8 on the auction-day close) gets a second out-of-sample print here. NO PRICE CHANNEL IS CLAIMED and impact is `low`: no tracked symbol carries yen-rates exposure and no house playbook is rates-keyed. The corridor around it is unusually loaded: fomc-2026-10-28 the day before, ecb-decision-2026-10-29, gdp-q3-2026-advance-2026-10-29 and pce-2026-10-29 on the day, and boj-decision-2026-10-30 the morning after — so this auction prices into the last Tokyo session before the BoJ, which is the sharpest coupon-setting test the rule will get. Estimate widens caution only; it licenses no date-keyed action.
